root_idea.summary: The root has two principal semantic fields: a distinctive poised or gathered stance, and a vessel or receptacle.
root_idea.development: The standing branch includes a horse raising one leg while the limbs are gathered, and extends to aligned feet and measured division of water. A separate vessel branch denotes skin containers and related objects; the vein sense is treated as an outlying lexical branch.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular active-participle citation form صَافِنٌ rather than the Quranic feminine plural form.

senses.definition: Of a horse: standing poised on three legs while raising the fourth, with the tip of its hoof touching the ground.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is the feminine plural صَافِنَاتٌ, describing horses in this distinctive standing posture.

senses.definition: In a reported Quranic variant reading concerning sacrificial animals: standing with one foreleg tied to the upper limb; the reading was also interpreted simply as standing or standing still.
senses.usage_conditions: This variant Quranic construction is recorded in the lexical evidence, but its modern verse location is not claimed here because no corresponding QAC location is supplied for it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Joining or bringing two things together, with one close against the other.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a general lexical description of the root’s gathering or compacting sense, distinct from the specific Quranic horse posture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stand with the feet set evenly or close together; of a person, to stand in this posture, especially in prayer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reports distinguish setting the feet evenly or close together from turning one foot backward in imitation of a horse’s stance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To compact dry herbage and leaves into a habitation or nest, or the resulting habitation made by a bird, hornet, or similar creature.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The habitation may be made for the creature itself or for its young.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To gather one’s clothes together upon a saddle or similar support.
To fling someone or something upon the ground.
To rend or slit the scrotal covering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is the anatomical noun صَفَنٌ, ‘scrotum’.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Standing in confrontation with a people or party.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the reciprocal or interactional noun مُصَافَنَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To divide a limited supply of water among people by measured shares, traditionally using a pebble to gauge each allotment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Each person’s portion could be measured as the amount covering the pebble placed in the vessel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A round skin or leather food cloth or spread, gathered near its edge by a drawstring so that it can form a bag.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The vocalization صَفْنٌ is reported with a qualification that it may be a variant or error for صُفْنٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A skin or leather receptacle, pouch, or small bucket used for provisions, utensils, travel equipment, or sometimes for drawing water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same term may refer to a vessel used for ablution; by metonymy, the water contained in such a vessel may also be called صُفْنٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The faucial pouch or throat sac of a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized anatomical usage distinct from the scrotum sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The envelope or sheath of an ear of corn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is used by comparison with the scrotum.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A saphenous or related vein, especially a vein in the leg or shank.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical descriptions vary as to the precise location, including veins of the shank, arm, thigh, or a deep vein extending along the spine.

cautions: The canonical QAC occurrence is the feminine plural صَافِنَاتٌ at 38:31; the reported variant Quranic reading concerning sacrificial animals is retained without assigning it an additional modern location.
Classical authorities differ on the precise anatomical location meant by صَافِنٌ in the vein sense.
